title: Perranti's band and Dave Lewenta
summary: Hug remembers clarinetist Perranti and pianist Dave Lewenta.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What about Perranti? Did you go around and listen to his band ever?

Perranti, yes. I can remember Perranti when he played at the Liberty Theater. He was a big man in those days. All the women and all the girls and everybody used to be running behind him, because he was really a real handsome looking guy, and played fine clarinet in those days. And I believe Perranti had a band at the La Vida, didn't he, at one time? That was right next door to the Fern Dance Hall. And we used to listen, we used to go next door, whenever we got somebody to sit in and play for us at the point, and we'd listen to his band, the La Vida. And I think he had a piano player with him by the name of Dave Lewenta. He was from, I forget where he was from, but he was a fine piano player. He's in Chicago now.
That was at the pump room you played last?
Yeah, he was at the pump room for years.
I don't know if he's still there or not, but he was a very, very fine piano player. Yeah, Tony Perranti, he used to listen to him quite a lot.
